transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-25
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Donnell (Redwood); Priya Raman, Carlos Mendes, Olivia Park, Jonas Erickson, Aisha Khanna (Solstice)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal intake to surface SLA exception requests, DPA redline path, and a short discussion about export controls / data residency for a pilot. AE + SE from Redwood; procurement/ security / engineering + legal/finance from Solstice. Outcome: agree next steps and owners for redlines and a technical deep dive on private deployment options.

Topics covered:
- DPA redline process and timeline
- SLA metrics, tail latency/SLOs and exceptions for high-sensitivity workloads
- Export controls and cross-border data residency for patient metadata
- VPC/private deployment vs hosted with contractual controls
- Pricing approval path and provisioning for a 3-month pilot
- Procurement PO, billing terms, and required security attachments (SOC2, ISO)

Action items (read out in call): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for squeezing this in today, um we wanted to run through where you are on procurement and a couple of legal asks before we push the pilot live
[00:09] Priya Raman: thanks Maya yeah, appreciate it, i'll try to be brief, we just want to make sure the DPA and SLA stuff is clear, and also there are some export control constraints from our legal team on the patient dataset so that's a blocker unless we map it out
[00:22] Liam O'Donnell: totally, and just to set expectations from our side: Redwood has hosted, dedicated and private deployment options. For regulated PHI workloads customers typically either go Private (VPC/on-prem) or Hosted with contractual restrictions — we can document both flows
[00:36] Carlos Mendes: and by export controls we mean specifically certain attributes cannot leave eu/europe datacenters, and for some data fields we need encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys and auditability, like key rotation logs, correct?
[00:50] Liam O'Donnell: yeah that's right, KM S/HSM integration is supported; we call out KMS options in our security pack. There might be some mis-grammar in the doc but we support both cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys for private deployments
[01:03] Olivia Park: quick question on SLA — our app requires below 200ms p95 for short prompts, is that realistic on hosted?
[01:11] Maya Chen: short answer: depends. Hosted can hit low latencies for small models and in-region traffic; but for large models and heavier prompt context you often want Dedicated or Private to guarantee throughput and tail latency. we can lay out the SLA tiers and delta for dedicated pools
[01:27] Jonas Erickson: and from finance i need to understand billing cadence. if we do a three-month pilot do you do monthly invoices or net-30 after PO? any early termination fee?
[01:38] Maya Chen: standard is monthly billing against usage for hosted; for dedicated/pilot we can do committed monthly invoice and propose an MOA that maps to a short term pilot commitment — we'll include proposed payment terms in the commercial worksheet
[01:50] [crosstalk] Priya Raman: we need the procurement intake doc that has the approver list — i can share that after this call
[01:56] Maya Chen: perfect, that helps. we usually need the approver matrix, tax details, and preferred PO routing
[02:05] [00:02:05] Carlos Mendes: circling back to the SLA exception: our security team will request an exception that any request that touches raw PHI must be routed to private deployment. can you outline what that boundary looks like? how is classification enforced?
[02:21] Liam O'Donnell: enforcement is a mix of policy + infra. we can route calls by tag or route, or at the org level pin model variants to private runtimes. for classification you'd still be responsible for tagging at the application layer — we provide routing policies and audit logs so you can prove to auditors which requests were served where
[02:39] Aisha Khanna: on the MSA side we have two asks: 1) we want the DPA redline today, and 2) we want to limit Redwood's subcontractors for the pilot; can we get a list of subprocessors and a clause that prohibits further subprocessing without notice?
[02:56] Maya Chen: we can produce a current subprocessor list; the MSA already has standard subprocessor language but we can discuss a limited-subprocessor addendum for pilots. i'll send the list and propose wording in the redline
[03:07] Priya Raman: also export control language — do you have standard clauses for data that cannot cross borders? we might need an exhibit that pins EU-only processing
[03:16] Liam O'Donnell: yes, we have data residency exhibits and we can include region restrictions for hosted; if you require EU-only then private deployment in EU region or on-prem is the best path, otherwise we can negotiate contractual commitments for region-limited processing
[03:31] Olivia Park: if we do private, what's the timeline to provision a dedicated pool or VPC? we need a rough lead time for our SRE planning
[03:40] Liam O'Donnell: dedicated pools are typically provisioned in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and approvals; private/VPC deployments can be 4-8 weeks if there's network setup and firewall rules, KMS provisioning can also add a week or two. this is rough, subject to capacity
[03:56] Jonas Erickson: do you have SOC2/ISO artifacts available to push to our compliance portal?
[04:01] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 Type II report and our security pack (pen test summary, ISO attestation) — we'll share the pack link and credentials for your reviewers, and we can arrange vendor attestation call if required
[04:12] [00:04:12] Priya Raman: great. about pricing: for a pilot we want a capped spend with a usage bank to prevent surprises. can you propose a pilot pricing that includes a cap and an overage rate?
[04:23] Maya Chen: absolutely, we usually propose a capped pilot invoice plus overage at a reduced rate. we'll put three options: low, medium, high cap with corresponding capacity reservation — i'll include that in the commercial worksheet
[04:35] Carlos Mendes: one more security detail: we require an audit log retention of 2 years and API-level tracing that ties back to token IDs. is that doable?
[04:46] Liam O'Donnell: yes, audit retention is configurable; we can export logs to your SIEM or retain in our console for the agreed window. token-level tracing is available, though we should clarify what you mean by token ID — we can map request IDs to tokens in the logs for tracing purposes
[05:00] Olivia Park: on data masking — can Redwood support automatic redaction for certain entity types before they hit the model?
[05:06] Liam O'Donnell: we have an ingestion layer where you can plug in pre-processing for redaction; for private deployments you can run that pre-processing in your VPC. hosted customers can use our prefix-caching and pre-process hooks but you'd need to accept that it runs in a hosted context
[05:20] [00:05:20] Aisha Khanna: does Redwood accept PO terms that reference a master subscription and attachables? we often prefer a single MSA + SOW approach and attach the DPA and SLA as exhibits
[05:31] Maya Chen: yes that's standard; MSA + exhibits (DPA, SLA, security pack) is the typical flow for enterprise. we can work with your standard signature authority and accept counterparty signature blocks
[05:40] Jonas Erickson: are there any early termination fees for pilot conversions into production?
[05:44] Maya Chen: for pilots we typically don't levy an early termination fee for short pilots; if there's reserved dedicated capacity then there may be pro-rated minimums — we'll call that out in the commercial worksheet
[05:54] Priya Raman: okay next i want to flag procurement approvals — we need a list of approvers and their thresholds. we'll attach that to the intake doc. can Redwood escalate pricing approvals internally to a named contact if we need faster signoff?
[06:07] Maya Chen: yes i'll be the named commercial contact, and i'll loop in finance leadership for pricing approvals if you provide the approver thresholds. i'll include escalation paths in the sheet
[06:17] [00:06:17] Carlos Mendes: on export controls again — we have a specific constraint from export compliance: some PII fields can't be processed outside of certain approved territories. does Redwood support field-level routing or do we need to filter at the application layer?
[06:33] Liam O'Donnell: we don't currently do automatic field-level routing; that's best handled at application layer or via a pre-processing hook. we can provide a recommended pattern and sample code for tagging requests and routing them to the correct runtime
[06:45] Aisha Khanna: we'd also like indemnity language for data breaches to be clarified — is Redwood willing to negotiate indemnity caps specific to regulated PHI?
[06:56] Maya Chen: we'll need to take that back to legal — standard MSA has liability caps, but we can surface the ask and propose language. i'll include that as an explicit redline request and put your legal contact in the thread
[07:07] Olivia Park: technical follow-up: what's the FIPS level for KMS integration in dedicated/private?
[07:12] Liam O'Donnell: we support FIPS 140-2 validated modules via certain KMS providers; for HSM we can support FIPS-level modules depending on the vendor — i'll call out vendor specifics in the technical deep dive doc
[07:23] [00:07:23] Jonas Erickson: re billing alerting — can you provide daily usage reports and threshold alerts to avoid surprises?
[07:29] Maya Chen: yep we have per-route token-level cost breakdowns and reporting; we can set up usage alerts and weekly reports for the pilot
[07:37] Priya Raman: workflow for sign-off — what do you need from us to move procurement forward?
[07:41] Maya Chen: procurement intake sheet, approver matrix, target PO timeline, and any redline prompts your legal wants prioritized. once we get that, we'll send the DPA/MAA redline and SLA matrix and propose the pilot commercial terms
[07:54] Carlos Mendes: will you include a subprocessor list with the redline? we need to check if any subprocessors are on our restricted vendor list
[07:59] Maya Chen: yes, subprocessor list will be attached. if there's a restricted vendor we can discuss alternatives or a narrowly-scoped addendum for the pilot
[08:07] [00:08:07] Aisha Khanna: timeline check — we need a signed pilot agreement before 2026-10-15 to meet internal go-live dates; is that feasible?
[08:16] Maya Chen: feasible if we move quickly — goal: redline and SLA matrix by 2026-10-02, procurement approvals by 2026-10-09, then sign by 2026-10-15. we'll treat the pilot paperwork as an expedited path
[08:29] Liam O'Donnell: i'll propose two technical deep-dive times next week; one focused on VPC/KMS/network and one on latency and model sizing for your p95 SLOs
[08:38] Olivia Park: good. can we also get a list of models and their verified latencies for p95 at different sequence lengths?
[08:45] Liam O'Donnell: yes, we have an internal performance matrix (redwood-verified) and i'll share a subset relevant to health workload patterns
[08:54] Maya Chen: perfect. quick note — we'll also add a break-glass fallback policy for capacity constraints: if dedicated capacity is constrained we can failover to a lower-latency-compatible variant or region as long as that's permitted in the DPA for the pilot. that will be in the SLA notes
[09:08] [00:09:08] Priya Raman: ok last item from procurement: invoice recipient and remittance details — i'll email the template after this call
[09:13] Maya Chen: thanks Priya. we'll pick up on the DPA redline and SLA matrix. Liam, any final technical callouts?
[09:20] Liam O'Donnell: just to reiterate, for PHI-sensitive flows private in-region or VPC is safest; we can provide architecture diagrams and sample IaC to expedite your SRE's setup
[09:30] Maya Chen: thanks everyone for the clarity. recap of next steps: maya sends DPA + SLA redline and commercial worksheet; liam sends tech docs and proposes deep-dive times; priya shares procurement intake and approver list.
[09:43] Priya Raman: we'll aim to get that intake doc to you by Tuesday and prioritize the redline comments internally
[09:49] Jonas Erickson: finance will review pilot pricing once it's on paper; expect us to push back on rounding and PO timing but we can be flexible
[09:55] Aisha Khanna: legal will compile exceptions list. i'll coordinate with carlos on export language specifics.
[10:02] Maya Chen: outstanding — i'll follow up with an email with attachments and calendar invites for the deep dive. appreciate everyone's time.
[10:08] [00:10:08] Meeting ends
